Fixes a flaky SECURITY test found while running the suite for an unrelated docs-only slice: tests/crew/test_session_credentials.py::test_cipher_rejects_tampering_and_wrong_key failed once then passed 5/5 in isolation. Root cause REPRODUCED, not inferred: the tampered value was built as ciphertext[:-1] + b'x', which overwrites the last byte instead of changing it, so whenever the ciphertext already ended in 0x78 the 'tampered' value was byte-identical to the original, decryption correctly succeeded, and pytest.raises failed -- roughly 1 run in 256. A reproduction hit the case on attempt 14 and showed byte-identical: True with decrypt returning no error. Fix: flip the final byte with XOR plus an explicit assert that the tamper changed something. Verified over 5000 fresh encryptions with zero failures to detect, 8/8 consecutive test runs, Ruff clean, full non-browser suite green at 1417 passed / 1 skipped. TEST-ONLY: no application behaviour, schema, provider, live-sync write or authority change; no preview restart needed because the app never imports tests. Filed as OS-062 (done). Fixes a defect I shipped: scripts/install_desktop_shortcut.command was committed with mode 100644 (no executable bit) and sat on disk as -rw-------, so double-clicking it in Finder failed with 'you do not have appropriate access privileges' and the owner could not install the Desktop preview launcher at all. This is the exact failure class the mission warns about: I verified the script EXISTED and never verified it could RUN, then told the owner to double-click it -- 'exists' treated as 'works'. Fixed with chmod 755 on both launchers AND git update-index --chmod=+x, because a fresh clone takes its modes from git rather than from the working tree, so a filesystem-only fix would have left the bug in the repository. Added tests/test_launcher_scripts.py (4 tests) asserting every tracked scripts/*.command and scripts/*.sh is executable in the WORKING TREE (what Finder executes) and IN GIT (what a clone materialises), and carries a shebang; FALSIFIED BEFORE TRUSTING IT -- reintroducing chmod 644 makes the working-tree test fail, restoring it passes all four. Also records an incident: a diagnostic loop over every tracked file timed out at 300 s and reset the persistent shell (second reset in this lane), so such checks must stay bounded by pathspec. No financial, provider, schema or authority change; the preview still needs STARTING by the owner, which is what the launcher is for.

BACKFILL ATTEMPTED (owner-approved) AND BLOCKED: all 5 Google refresh tokens fail with HTTP 400, detected before any fetch, so the store was NOT damaged (732 items / 0 blobs unchanged). Likely cause -- tokens minted 2026-09-06, 14 days old, and Google expires refresh tokens after 7 days while the OAuth consent screen is in 'Testing' status -- but this must be CONFIRMED in the Google Cloud console, not assumed. Owner action: re-authorize once, and publish the OAuth app to production to stop it recurring. No secrets printed. EXTENDED: token-health signal (per-kind credential failures classified into actionable reasons, bounded detail, copy-on-read, cleared only on real authentication) plus per-account Gmail resilience behind an optional callback so one dead token no longer hides the rest; and iCloud added to the poll cycle (it was reachable only by hand, so forwarded mail would have sat unread). 11 new tests, falsified three ways. SCOPE EXTENDED to the Connections surface (service, API route, app getter, JS, CSS) and its tests, because surfacing credential health required threading it from the poll service to the row the owner reads. FORWARDED-MAIL PROVENANCE: Gmail forwarding replaces From (verified against the owner's real forwarded Eversource bill -- 44 headers, none carrying the original sender; the domain survives only in the body's quoted From). gmail_intake.py now recovers it in a bounded way and carries it in the stored title so the bill matcher works unchanged, with the stored sender still reporting what actually arrived. 8 new tests, including a wiring test kept alongside the matcher test because falsification showed the matcher test alone stays green. MEASURED THE RUNNING SYSTEM and found two defects: IMAP4_SSL had no timeout (a stall hung the daemon poll invisibly forever) and credential health shared the poll's long-held lock (the Connections page could block behind a running poll, likely the empty-list the owner saw). Both fixed with tests. MAILBOX SELECTOR: fetch_recent/ingest_icloud_recent take a mailbox (default INBOX for compatibility) and app.py wires MERIDIAN_ICLOUD_MAILBOX, so intake can read a dedicated bill folder; a missing folder RAISES rather than silently falling back to the inbox, because silent fallback would ingest personal mail. READ-ONLY HARDENING after a real mistake: an IMAP APPEND probe wrote sieve text into the owner's INBOX; located by UID and deleted+expunged. The transport now declares forbidden mutating commands with assert_read_only_command(), and a behavioral test drives a fetch against a recording fake asserting no mutating verb is issued (falsified with a deliberate connection.store()). Gmail filters could NOT be created: the Composio token lacks gmail.settings.basic (403), so filter creation is owner-only. EVIDENCE VIEWER ERROR PAGE: a browser navigation to missing evidence now gets readable HTML instead of raw JSON (Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate), while JSON clients keep the structured error. Measured 2026-09-21: 46 of 775 mail items have stored content; 729 do not, so most invoice links point at a document that was never persisted. INGEST ORDER FIXED: ingest_record wrote the metadata row BEFORE the blob and swallowed blob-write failures, so a row could promise content it did not have -- the structural cause of 729 unopenable items. Content is now written first, a failure aborts the ingest, and a missing blob store is refused. The readiness probe now asserts the invariant instead of letting the synthetic failure propagate. CHARGE MATCHING: new meridian/charge_match.py matches evidence to the charge it documents on a verifiable basis (amount + date), records ambiguity instead of resolving it, and never mutates a transaction. Owner correction acted on: Gmail is directly readable via Composio, so missing local blobs are irrelevant -- verified by fetching two real OpenAI $8.00 invoices whose bodies match two ledger charges on 2026-09-18. BACKFILL: rewired the old bare-amount matcher to require DATE corroboration (270 links from 45 receipts -> 9, all verified), and executed the backfill through the canonical pipeline with a DB backup. Live: items 777->822, blobs 46->91, 9 high-confidence receipt-to-charge links.

OS-113: identify the spend pocket from Crew's OWN SELECTION instead of an English name, with the two-name allow-list kept as a NAMED fallback (owner decisions, 2026-09-25: selection becomes authoritative; the fallback stays and must name itself). Ledger limits honoured: no provider write, no deployment, no new name PATTERN, and the migration ships only because the owner approved it explicitly. Evidence for the slice is verified against artifacts, not records: readback_selected_spend_pocket() run over the owner's real historical capture returns exactly one id (Subaccount:edc8cb88-...) with no ambiguity, and that id is byte-identical to financial_accounts.external_id in both readable databases -- the row named 'Safe to Spend' (active) in gate.db, and the row named 'Free to Spend' in the older savings_data.db under the SAME id, which is the rename itself. The name mechanism is measurably ambiguous in BOTH databases: gate.db matches two rows ('Safe to Spend' active and 'Free to Spend' inactive), and savings_data.db matches two ACTIVE pockets both named 'Free to Spend' that no name-based rule can tell apart. Supersedes the generation-8 claim os111-safe-to-spend-single-rule-20260925 for these files; the OS-111 claim's money rule is unchanged and its own files stay untouched here except where this slice threads the resolution through.
claims.description: OS-113 -- which pocket the owner spends from comes from Crew's OWN SELECTION (userSpendConfig.selectedSpendSubaccount), matched by Crew's id, with the two-name allow-list kept as a NAMED fallback. Adds migration 030 and the observed-selection store, and threads the resolution through Today, Plan and the dial.
